overview.overview:
Arizona has moved from a narrow Democratic win in 2020, when Biden carried it by about half a point, to a Republican margin of roughly five and a half points in 2024. That shift leaves the state about four points more Republican than the nation as a whole. With the national environment favoring Democrats by nearly five points, the forecast expects Arizona to land close to even, with a slight Democratic edge of about one point.

The state's 11 electoral votes are competitive but unlikely to be decisive: the estimated odds that Arizona is the tipping-point state are around seven percent. The plausible range is wide, spanning from a solid Republican win to a clear Democratic one.
overview.watch: Whether Arizona's 2024 rightward shift proves durable or reverts toward its 2020 competitiveness will determine if the state stays near even or tilts clearly to one side.
key_factors: Arizona's rightward shift in 2024 leaves it about four points Republican-leaning relative to the nation
A favorable national environment for Democrats offsets that lean and produces a near-even expected margin
Mark Kelly's presence on the Democratic ticket as an Arizona home-state candidate could add a small local advantage
Wide uncertainty means either side could carry the state comfortably
